# Blueprint v0.3.6 — hardware-aware planning, multi-GPU serving, and an Optimize step

Planning and serving now understand your actual GPUs — including splitting a
model across several of them — and the wizard gains a proper Optimize step.

## Fit badges now reflect your real hardware

The Plan step used to compare a model against a single VRAM number. It now sizes
against your **detected per-GPU VRAM + system RAM** and tells you *how* each model
would run:

- **Runs on this machine** — fits one GPU with headroom.
- **Tight fit** / **tight — trim context** — fits, but close, or needs a shorter
  context / KV offload.
- **Runs across N GPUs** — too big for one GPU, but your GPUs together hold it
  (see multi-GPU below).
- **Mostly CPU — slow** — weights don't fit VRAM but do fit RAM.
- **Needs more VRAM** — genuinely won't fit at this quant/context.

The header line reads e.g. *"Sizing fit against your hardware: 1 GPU · 6 GB VRAM
detected."* Red now means "won't run," not "needs a bit of tuning."

## Multi-GPU serving

When a model is too big for a single GPU but fits across the ones you have,
Blueprint now **splits it automatically** — generating llama.cpp's
`--split-mode` / `--tensor-split` flags proportional to each GPU's VRAM. No
configuration required; single-GPU machines are unaffected.

## New Optimize step in the install wizard

The wizard is now **Plan → Hardware → Optimize → Deploy**. The Optimize step lets
you set the weight quantization and context window, plus a single **GPU
placement** control:

- It shows the automatic plan read-only (e.g. *"Runs on 1 GPU — 3.9 GB used"*).
- An **Advanced** disclosure lets experts override — GPU-layer offload, and, on
  multi-GPU machines, the split mode (layer/row) — with **Reset to auto** always
  a click away.

## Under the hood

- A new placement engine (unit-tested) drives both the fit badges and the serve
  flags, so what Plan shows and what Deploy runs stay consistent.
- Groundwork toward managing LLMs on remote machines has begun landing internally;
  nothing user-facing yet.

## Other platforms

All of this lives in the shared frontend + serve path, so macOS and Linux get it
too.
